changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 2 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/6625-retire-fieldmeta-decimals.md`

- names `GridField.tsx` → `packages/fields/src/widgets/GridField.tsx` — edited by this change

  > `buildFieldMeta` computed `decimals: overrides.decimals ?? meta?.decimals ?? meta?.scale` on **every** call and the value **reached nothing**. Re-measured on this branch's base (`efdc6c62`): **zero `.decimals` member reads** across `@object-ui/fields`, `@object-ui/i18n`, `@object-ui/components`, `@object-ui/core` and `plugin-dashboard` itself — the only non-comment occurrence was the write being removed here. The **positive control in the same query shape** fires: `.scale` member reads hit `NumberField.tsx`, `GridField.tsx` and `fields/src/index.tsx`. So the zero is a finding, not a broken query. The `overrides.decimals ??` head of that chain had already lost its only feeder when objectui#6425's ruling removed the authored read from `ObjectDataTable.enrich()`; `RecordDetailDrawer`, the only other `buildFieldMeta` caller, passes no overrides at all. Both halves retire together, so the key leaves in one move.

### `.changeset/6661-app-launcher-nav-menu-renderers.md`

- names `en.ts` → `packages/i18n/src/locales/en.ts` — edited by this change

  > Three new strings — the launcher's and the menu's accessible names, and the menu's empty state — are declared under `console.nav` in `en.ts` and its nine sibling packs. An inline `defaultValue` alone is not a fix: it renders English at one call site and leaves the string untranslatable everywhere (objectui#3517).

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Compared the checked-out tree with `ce26f401f` (merge-base with origin/main): 17 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1782 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (2389 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/36658649731)

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `9337738d7a5462423123f9bbce53fe0f9cf83e0c`

Inputs: card objectui#11160 (body; triage `5901928489`, claim `5902330695`, dev report `5902729745`), PR objectui#11169 (body, its 18-file list, the net diff against `main` at the head), the head's check-runs (`filter=latest`), plus file reads at the head and at the base `ce26f401f` for context. Read-only: no worktree, no build, no test run, no gate re-run.

**Check-runs on the head (the gate verdicts).** 43 runs, every one completed (I waited: Test shards 1-8, Type Check and Spec Main Shape Gate were in progress when I started and finished at 02:24Z): 40 success, 3 skipped (dependabot, Test (coverage), Test (coverage shard)), 0 failure. Named: Lint, Type Check, Test (shards 1-8), Test (dist pins), Build & E2E, Bundle Analysis, Docs Route Eager Closure Check, Changeset Declaration / Bump Policy / Claim Re-read / Fixed Group Check / Overwrite Report, Line Citation Gate, Control Byte Scan, Inert vi.mock Specifier Check, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec Main Shape Gate, Live E2E (informational).

### ① Derived judgments

**Cells: right.**
- One expression. `requiredCellText(c)` is defined once in `GridField`'s body (`GridField.tsx:668-669`) and is the only producer at all three sites (`:1111` lookup `error`, `:1131` file `error`, `:1348` plain `title`). No third copy of the template, no new key: `validation.required` already sits in every pack (en `:201` `{{field}} is required`, zh `:167` `{{field}}不能为空`).
- `{{field}}` is `c.label || c.name`, the expression the old `${c.label || c.name} is required` used, so en is byte-equal at each site whether the column has a label or not.
- The inline `defaultValue` `'{{field}} is required'` equals the en pack value, and it is load-bearing: `useFieldTranslation` is `createSafeTranslation(FIELD_DEFAULTS, ...)` and `FIELD_DEFAULTS` carries no `validation.required` row, so with no provider `fallbackT` falls to the inline default and `interpolateFallback` fills `{{field}}` (`useSafeTranslation.ts:48-57`). `check:i18n-keys` holds that default to en (the dev's positive control). Under a provider `createI18n` sets `escapeValue: false` (`i18n.ts:237`), so a label with `&` or a quote renders as written, as the old template literal did.

**Hints: right.**
- All three read `useFormChromeTranslation` (`MasterDetailForm.tsx:684`) at `:771`, `:794`, `:818`, keys `form.masterDetail.noChildObject` / `schemaUnavailable` / `noRelationshipField`.
- en byte-equal. I reconstructed each old literal's text content from the base (`MasterDetailForm.tsx:746-747`, `:767-769`, `:790-794` at `ce26f401f`; JSX collapses its line breaks to single spaces) and filled the en value's holes with the same values: all three are equal. The three `formChrome.ts` rows (`:70-77`) equal the en pack values character for character (99 / 142 / 195 characters).
- Ten packs (ar, de, en, es, fr, ja, ko, pt, ru, zh) each carry the three keys; every hole is present in every pack (`{{property}}`; `{{object}}`; `{{object}}` `{{parent}}` `{{property}}`), and `lookup` / `master_detail` stay as written in all ten.
- Key placement: a fair reading. "Its own key beside `form.lineItems.noChildObject`" asks for a distinct key with en unchanged; `form.masterDetail.noChildObject` is distinct, is the twin leaf, and sits in the namespace the master-detail form's other chrome and the other two hints already read (`formChrome.ts` is their one reader); in every pack `masterDetail` is the block directly above `lineItems`. The en sentences stay distinct ("collection" / "panel").
- Reuse search: holds. Over the en pack the nearest is `excelImport.schemaReadFailed` (`Could not read the object schema.`, `:3543`), which names no object, no consequence and no remedy; `form.errorLoading` (`:330`) is a heading; `importMappingsUnavailable` / `savedViewsUnavailable` (`:1875`, `:1878`) are about other things; nothing states a missing relationship field. No existing key carries either hint's meaning, so two new keys is the direction's "otherwise add keys in all ten packs".
- `withCodeHoles` (`MasterDetailForm.tsx:607-615`): right under a provider and without one. Under a provider `t(key, { property: '{{property}}' })` fills the hole with its own spelling; i18next's default `skipOnVariables` (true) does not re-scan the inserted value, and `escapeValue: false` leaves it alone (i18next's escaper touches no brace anyway). Without a provider `fallbackT` reads the `formChrome.ts` row and `interpolateFallback` splits on `{{property}}` and joins with `{{property}}`, a no-op (`fallbackInterpolation.ts:103`). The helper then splits on a capturing alternation of the named holes, so every separator becomes a code element in whatever order the locale puts it (the ja pin has a leading hole). Hole values never pass through `t`, so no escaping setting can alter an authored object name; the regex is built from the three fixed names only.
- Second copy? Partly. `LineItemsPanel.tsx:715-717` does the one-hole form inline (`t(...).split('{{property}}')` into before / after). `withCodeHoles` generalises it, and both live in `packages/plugin-form/src`, so a shared module would have needed no public export; but pointing the panel at it would have touched `LineItemsPanel.tsx`, which the claim's file surface excludes. A note, not a finding: a follow-up may move the helper beside `formChrome.ts` and fold the panel's split into it.

**Pins against the direction: right.**
- zh render of each of the six sites: the plain cell's `title` (`Qty不能为空`); the lookup and file cells' `error` (observed at the prop through wrapped modules whose specifiers `./LookupField` / `./FileField` match `GridField.tsx:22-23`) and their `title`; the three hints' full text and the text of each code element in order.
- en control, byte-equal: under a provider (both files) and with none (the two `.no-provider` files, each its own file so no earlier provider mount answers it).
- authored / server message unchanged: the authored zh label `数量` fills the hole as written and a label-less column falls back to its name; the authored object names `po_line` / `purchase_order` render as code; the schema-unavailable arm keeps the thrown server error out of the DOM (the pin asserts `SCHEMA_UNAVAILABLE` is absent).
- Reverse verification: 9 red / 6 green is the arithmetic of the four files (GridField zh: 5 red + the en control green; GridField no-provider: 1 green; MasterDetailForm zh: 4 red, ja included, + the en control green; no-provider: 3 green), the en controls green, which is what "en byte-equal to the old literals" predicts.

**Closure.** The six sites are the ones the card enumerates, and the diff introduces no other user-facing literal in the two files. The family's last card is closed by this diff.

### ② Semver level

`Clause-②: no` is right. No export, prop, type or accepted set moves: `withCodeHoles` is module-local, `requiredCellText` is component-local, `FORM_CHROME_DEFAULTS` is not exported, and the only published change is three additive keys in the `@object-ui/i18n` packs with en byte-equal to what rendered before. The changeset `.changeset/11160-line-items-last-english.md` is `patch` on `@object-ui/fields`, `@object-ui/i18n` and `@object-ui/plugin-form`: the three packages with source changes, and the family's precedent (`11131-line-items-chrome.md`, `11145-line-items-chrome-remainder.md`, the same three at patch). Its paragraph describes the diff. Changeset Declaration, Bump Policy, Claim Re-read and Fixed Group Check: success on the head.

### ③ Boundary flags

`open_questions`: none declared. Deviations (3), each answered:
1. Attribution trailer: the harness reminder and objectui AGENTS.md differ; the dev followed the repo's model-free pair. Not a deviation from the order; recorded, fine.
2. Gates beyond the order's list were run (the vi.mock trio, test-path-roots, unreferenced-sources, self-import, pending-changeset-literals, i18n-dead-keys), and `check:eager-locale-catalogues` was NOT MEASURED for lack of a console build. Answered by the head's check-runs: Docs Route Eager Closure Check and Bundle Analysis are success.
3. Worktree removed after the PR opened. Housekeeping, fine.

Out-of-scope note (a), `submitViaBatch`: real. `MasterDetailForm.tsx:1649` at the head throws `Error('This save was not sent: another save of this form was still in progress.')`. It reaches the screen by source reading: `ObjectForm.tsx:1272` awaits `schema.submitHandler`, its catch (`:1440-1444`) calls `schema.onError` (the form's `handleError`, which does not toast) and rethrows; the components form renderer's catch (`renderers/form/form.tsx:2515-2526`) resolves `extractWriteErrorMessage(error)`, which returns a plain Error's message unchanged (`error-message.ts`: neither strip pattern matches this sentence), then `setSubmitError` (the in-form banner) and `toast.error`. Reach is narrow: the Save button is guarded, so only an implicit header submission (Enter in a single-text-input header) during an in-flight batch gets there, and it was not measured in a render. Escalated to the seat as a card candidate: a class (a) card needs the one measurement the filing gate asks for, and the triage's closure rule sends it to a fresh card, not this one. Not a finding against this PR.

Out-of-scope note (b), dormant `error` text: right. `LookupField.tsx:258` takes `error` as `fieldError` and its only read is `aria-invalid={!!fieldError}` (`:1365`); `FileCell`'s `error` doc (`FileField.tsx:466-480`) says the message text stays with the cell's `title`, and its only read is `aria-invalid={!!error}` (`:577`). So neither component displays the text it is handed today, and that prop is what the card's sites 2 and 3 name (confirmed at source on the card, not measured). The pins still measure the direction's "zh render" for those cells: the visible text of a lookup or file cell is the same td `title`, which the zh pins assert for `product` and `receipt` too, and `aria-invalid` is a user-facing state for assistive tech. Proportionate; no finding.
